thread:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing a sudden spike of OOMs on prod GPUs at ~15:02 UTC. A bunch of requests hit kernel=matmul_v2 and the allocator failed with fragmented space.

runtime-bot: [alert] GPU OOM on node gpu-prod-12, pid 4421, kernel matmul_v2. Allocator high-water 10.8GB (16GB), fragmentation ~28%.

aj: Copying quick profile from the incident run. Kernel mem per-call looks up ~350MB higher than baseline. KV cache resident pages increased after the batch size bump yesterday.

maria: Here's the quick repro trace I grabbed (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18T15:02:12Z] matmul_v2::launch -> 350MB delta
[2026-03-18T15:02:12Z] allocator::alloc workspace 1024MB -> FAILED
[2026-03-18T15:02:12Z] kvcache::pages_resident +42% after user-batch tweak
```

aj: Sounds like two simultaneous regressions: (1) kernel selector picked a memory-heavy matmul path (maybe autotune tweak), (2) batching heuristic increase amplified KV working set.

maria: Agreed. Traffic is pretty normal, but we rolled the batching heuristic at 14:50. Reverting would be safest but we need a short mitigation plan.

devon: Suggested quick mitigation checklist:
- route traffic for the affected model to mem-optimized kernel selector (selector=mem-slim-v1).
- throttle max_batch_tokens -> 512 for that model route.
- enable allocator soft_reserve and reuse_buffers flags on the fleet.
- force KV TTL=30s for non-hot prefixes to shed cache.

maria: Can you post the exact flags? I can flip them on the fleet control plane now.

devon: Sure. CLI snippets:
```
redwoodctl route update --model prod-embedder:v12 --kernel-selector mem-slim-v1
redwoodctl config set --flag allocator.soft_reserve=true --flag runtime.reuse_buffers=true
redwoodctl route update --model prod-embedder:v12 --max_batch_tokens=512
redwoodctl kv update --model prod-embedder:v12 --default-ttl=30s
```

aj: Also enable a circuit breaker to fail fast for requests that exceed workspace budget: `circuit.breaker.workspace_bytes=9000000000` (9GB) and `fallback.model=prod-embedder:quant8` so we have a low-memory variant to fall back to.

runtime-bot: Deploying temporary mem-slim kernel selector to pool gpu-prod-group-2 (canary=20%).

sre-ops: We'll spin an extra node in the dedicated pool while the rollback is staged, scaling +1 node. If mitigation fails we can redirect 10% of traffic to dedicated-ssd fallback nodes.

maria: Implementing flags and throttle now. I'll watch for new OOM alerts and paste results in 5m.

aj: When this stabilizes we need a postmortem action items list: revert autotune change, add unit perf tests that assert per-kernel mem delta < 50MB, and add KV cache growth guard in the batching heuristic.

devon: Agreed. Also add a runtime telemetry metric for `kernel_selector.reason` so we can detect when mem-heavy kernels are chosen.

maria: Update — after setting reuse_buffers + mem-slim selector and throttling max_batch_tokens, OOMs dropped to 0 within two minutes. No user-facing errors so far.

maria: Next steps: I'll open a follow-up thread for a postmortem with perf traces and a rollback timeline. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
